externalBlockers.resource: A dedicated isolated execution worker — a separate Fly.io application or machine pool that can run a container runtime, distinct from the xroga-api app.
externalBlockers.purpose: Section 7 requires generated code to execute in a disposable, network-denied, unprivileged sandbox. The API host has no nested container runtime, so provider selection always returns unavailable in production and every executable validation refuses — which is the designed behaviour, not a gap.
externalBlockers.whyNotCreated: Creating it is a new billable Fly resource, which is outside the approved budget. Per the standing instruction, all code, config, tests and documentation were completed instead and the requirement is marked external_blocker.
externalBlockers.workCompletedAgainstIt: M7 shipped the provider-neutral registry (sandboxProviders.ts): preference ordering, a probe before every use, the full isolation flag set, and refusals that name every provider tried. M11 shipped the concrete hosted provider that registry had only left a seam for (remoteSandbox.ts): an HTTP worker client that sends the caller's scrubbed environment rather than process.env, puts its token in a header rather than a query string, requires HTTPS off loopback, and reads every non-conforming reply as 'not run' rather than success. configureRemoteSandboxProvider() runs at startup and registers it only when XROGA_SANDBOX_WORKER_URL is set, so the module is inert and costs nothing until an operator configures a worker. R2.13's two named tests — sentinel-secret isolation and network denial — now exist and pass against a stub worker. 56 sandbox tests pass. Attaching a real worker is configuration, not code.
externalBlockers.consequence: Command 1 cannot be reported as command_1_verified while this remains open.

nextAction: Owner decision required: approve a dedicated isolated-execution worker (a new paid Fly app or machine pool) to close R7.6 and R2.13. Once it exists, set XROGA_SANDBOX_WORKER_URL (and optionally XROGA_SANDBOX_WORKER_TOKEN) on xroga-api and restart — the API registers and probes it automatically. No implementation work is outstanding.
